name: Narrative Handoff Contract Rubric
description: Evaluation criteria for an architecture object passed between a structural agent and a drafting agent. Minimum standard: average score >= 3.5, with Evidence Binding and Absence Handling both >= 4.

criteria.name: Evidence Binding
criteria.description: Whether every non-absent slot and every scene traces to claim IDs that resolve to external artifacts

scores.1: Slots carry assertions with no evidence array at all; the contract is decorative
scores.2: Some slots cite evidence; others carry a confident sentence and nothing else
scores.3: Every slot cites evidence, but pointers are informal and some do not resolve
scores.4: Every slot and scene cites resolvable claim IDs; no pointer resolves into the pipeline's own output
scores.5: As 4, plus source dates recorded per slot and source interest annotated, so a starting weakness can be checked against a pre-outcome source

criteria.name: Absence Handling
criteria.description: Whether unfillable slots are declared and dispositioned rather than invented

scores.1: Every slot is filled; nothing is marked ABSENT and no gaps are recorded
scores.2: Gaps are mentioned in prose but carry no status field and no disposition
scores.3: Slots are marked ABSENT but several lack an empty_slot_move
scores.4: Every ABSENT slot carries a move, every gap carries one of the four dispositions, and no gap is left as 'draft and flag'
scores.5: As 4, plus the inference budget is respected (at most one INFERRED slot, never the climax) and each inference is disclosed in the body

criteria.name: Layer Discipline
criteria.description: Whether the structural layer stopped at the scene weave instead of drafting

scores.1: The architecture contains drafted paragraphs; the drafting agent inherits text to edit
scores.2: Scene entries run to several sentences of near-prose
scores.3: Scene lines are mostly short but a few exceed the cap
scores.4: Every tagged_line is within the cap and construction fields carry the detail
scores.5: As 4, and the validator was run and passed before the handoff was made

criteria.name: Provenance and Reproducibility
criteria.description: Whether the run can be re-derived, diffed, and audited later

scores.1: No run header; nothing records what produced this
scores.3: Model and corpus reference present, but no record of which claims were consulted
scores.4: Full run header including the coverage receipt of claim IDs actually consulted
scores.5: As 4, plus claims skipped are named explicitly, so partial coverage is visible rather than silent

criteria.name: Causal Typing
criteria.description: Whether causal claims carry a tier and stay inside the verbs that tier licenses

scores.1: No causal tiers; warrants assert causation freely
scores.2: Tiers assigned inconsistently, and warrants ignore them
scores.3: Every slot carries a tier, but some warrants exceed it
scores.4: Every tier is assigned and every warrant stays inside its permitted verbs
scores.5: As 4, plus no later reference upgrades a claim's tier anywhere in the artifact

criteria.name: The Dead Column
criteria.description: Whether killed findings are retained and the contradicting ones distinguished

scores.1: No dead column; killed findings were deleted
scores.2: A list of discarded items with no reasons
scores.3: Reasons recorded but 'did not support' and 'contradicted' are not distinguished
scores.4: Every entry carries what killed it and which of the two categories it falls in
scores.5: As 4, and every CONTRADICTED entry is routed into the deliverable rather than pruned

criteria.name: Return Channel
criteria.description: Whether the drafting layer can send a defect back up, and whether escalations were routed

scores.1: No escalation mechanism; the pipeline runs one way only
scores.2: Escalations arrive as prose notes with nothing to route them
scores.3: Escalation objects exist but do not name a layer
scores.4: Escalations carry beat, layer, defect and what would resolve it, and are recorded in the artifact
scores.5: As 4, and architecture-layer escalations produced a spine version bump and a re-pass rather than a local patch

criteria.name: Handoff Legibility
criteria.description: Whether the manifest survives being read by an agent that inherits nothing

scores.1: Refers to 'the architecture we built' and 'the next section'; unusable without the prior conversation
scores.2: Relative paths and an implied scope
scores.3: Absolute paths, but scope is described rather than enumerated
scores.4: Absolute paths, explicit beat IDs, an out-of-scope statement, and the required return shape
scores.5: As 4, plus a precondition check the downstream agent runs first and a style contract with a stated precedence order
